mn_electron_trap.mechanism: high-valence B-site Mn traps electrons and suppresses Ti4+ -> Ti3+ reduction, lowering electronic leakage
mn_electron_trap.relation: fewer free electrons -> lower conductivity sigma = n e mu
mn_electron_trap.source: Smyth, The Defect Chemistry of Metal Oxides (2000)

mn_acceptor_vacancy.mechanism: acceptor Mn on Ti sites is compensated by oxygen vacancies, raising ionic conduction
mn_acceptor_vacancy.relation: Kroger-Vink: Mn_Ti'' compensated by V_O^.. ; more V_O -> higher conduction

mn_soft_domains.mechanism: moderate Mn promotes ferroelectric domain formation (soft-like), raising Pr

mn_acceptor_hardening.mechanism: acceptor defect dipoles clamp domain walls (classic hardening)
mn_acceptor_hardening.relation: domain-wall pinning raises Ec and lowers Pr
mn_acceptor_hardening.source: Jaffe, Cook & Jaffe (1971); Carl & Hardtl, Ferroelectrics 17 (1978) 473
